compiled:
📰 General

Trump’s Afghanistan Comments Spark UK Outrage, Demand for Apology •

British Prime Minister Keir Starmer criticized U.S. President Donald Trump’s claim that non-U.S. NATO forces avoided frontline combat in Afghanistan. Starmer argued that Trump’s statement was inaccurate and disrespectful to the sacrifices made by allied troops. The UK government expressed concern over the potential damage to transatlantic relations caused by the remark. The incident highlights a growing rift between the U.S. and its NATO partners regarding the conduct of the war.

🌍 World

Merz Rejects Trump’s “Board of Peace,” Signals Openness to US Dialogue •

German Chancellor Friedrich Merz announced he would not participate in US President Donald Trump’s proposed “Board of Peace.” Merz stated that Germany remains open to exploring alternative forms of communication and cooperation with the United States. The initiative, announced by Trump, aims to establish a group of international leaders to discuss the war in Ukraine. German officials have expressed reservations regarding the board’s structure and potential implications.

🦅 US

Snooki Reveals Cancerous Cells Found in Cervix, Faces Potential Hysterectomy •

Nicole “Snooki” Polizzi, formerly known as Snooki, has revealed that a recent biopsy uncovered cancerous cells in her cervix. The 38-year-old reality television personality is now scheduled for a second biopsy as a result of the findings. Doctors are considering a possible hysterectomy as a treatment option. Polizzi expressed her fear regarding the diagnosis and the potential medical procedures she will need to undergo.

💰 Business

Bipartisan Bill Aims to Regulate Hemp Products, Reversing Trump’s THC Ban •

A new bipartisan bill introduced in Congress seeks to establish regulations for consumable hemp products. This legislation represents a shift from the 2022 spending bill signed by President Donald Trump, which implemented a complete ban on THC in hemp products. The proposed bill would allow for the production and sale of hemp-derived goods containing THC, provided they meet specific regulatory standards. Lawmakers argue this approach offers a more nuanced approach to hemp regulation compared to the previous, restrictive measure. The bill is currently under consideration in the House Energy and Commerce Committee.

💻 Technology

Xbox Reveals Strategic Reasons Behind “Day One” Game Releases on PS5 •

In a recent interview, Xbox Game Studios head Craig Duncan explained the differing approach to releasing games on PlayStation 5. The company strategically chooses titles for “day one” releases on PS5 to capitalize on the console’s strong initial demand and attract players. These releases typically involve games that benefit from immediate access to a large audience and enhanced marketing opportunities. Duncan clarified that not all Xbox titles are immediately available on PS5, reflecting a calculated decision based on market analysis and strategic priorities. This approach allows Xbox to maintain a competitive advantage and target specific player segments.

🎭 Entertainment

Zendaya Dominates Met Gala, Showcasing Stunning Custom Valentino Gown •

Zendaya graced the 2024 Met Gala with a breathtaking custom Valentino Haute Couture gown designed by Pierpaolo Piccioli. The dress featured a dramatic, floor-length silhouette with intricate embellishments and a deep V-neckline. She accessorized with Tiffany & Co. jewelry and a stunning diamond bracelet. The appearance marked a significant moment for the actress and the Valentino brand.

🏅 Sports

Ex-NFL Star Kevin Johnson Fatally Stabbed in Los Angeles Homeless Encampment •

Former Philadelphia Eagles and Oakland Raiders defensive lineman Kevin Johnson was fatally stabbed on Friday in a Los Angeles homeless encampment. Authorities confirmed that Johnson was attacked and subsequently died from his injuries. The incident occurred within a large encampment in the city’s Skid Row area. Investigations are currently underway to determine the circumstances surrounding the attack and identify the suspect(s).

🔬 Science

Three Major Space Missions Set to Launch This Year: Moon, Mars, and Beyond •

NASA’s Artemis II mission is scheduled for launch this year, marking the first crewed return to lunar orbit since the Apollo program. Simultaneously, Japan’s SLIM lander is preparing for a historic attempt to achieve the first-ever soft landing on the Moon. These missions represent significant advancements in space exploration, aiming to conduct scientific research and potentially pave the way for future long-term human presence in space. The projects are fueled by substantial international investment and a growing focus on robotic and human exploration of our solar system.

🩺 Health

Measles Cases Surge to 416 Across 14 U.S. States, CDC Reports •

The Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) announced Friday that the total number of measles cases in the United States has surpassed 400. A significant increase of 245 new cases were reported, bringing the total to 416. The outbreaks are currently concentrated in 14 states, with Arizona and California among those experiencing the highest numbers of infections. Public health officials are working to investigate the source of the outbreaks and implement preventative measures, including vaccination campaigns.
